proc effectiveScheme(req: var Request; trustProxy = false): string {.
    ...raises: [KeyError], tags: [], forbids: [].}

Returns the effective request scheme (http or https).

The powpow backend serves plain HTTP, so a direct connection is always http. When the app runs behind a reverse proxy (e.g. nginx with proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;) and trustProxy is true, the X-Forwarded-Proto header (first value wins) or the RFC 7239 Forwarded: proto= parameter decides instead. With trustProxy = false proxy headers are ignored so a spoofed X-Forwarded-Proto cannot flip the Secure cookie decision.

proc shouldEmitSecure(req: var Request; mode: CookieSecureMode;
                      trustProxy = false): bool {....raises: [KeyError], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}
Whether a Set-Cookie response for this request should carry the Secure attribute. secureAuto (default) emits it only over HTTPS, so plain http://localhost development cookies (which Safari drops when marked Secure, unlike Chrome/Firefox) keep working, while proxied HTTPS traffic still gets Secure.
